summary: Tested pricing bands, tiers, band-scoped fee rules, per-tender fee plan (charge/waive, payer), publish gates, award fee (raise/compute/cap/nil/waive/resend/list) and per-supplier fee plan, on both the backend and the frontend. Backend: 14/14 pytest tests passed. Frontend: every requested flow worked in the admin console (Masters > Pricing bands, Fee rules band scope, Notices publish checklist > FeePlanPanel, Billing > Award fees, Registrations > supplier fee choice, Ask PMC chat-toggle). Resend link created a real Stripe test checkout session from the backend, so the Stripe key works in this preview. Only the Resend email key is invalid, which is an existing environment issue.

minor.issue: bands values are not checked against pricing_bands. bands:['NOSUCHBAND'] is accepted (200) and saves a rule that never matches. Reject unknown band codes with 422.

For percentage rules, currency is taken from bid.price_currency, but pct_max and nil_below are in the rule's currency. If the bid currency differs from the rule currency, the cap and nil threshold are applied in the wrong currency.
winner_fee_pct is set from the first percentage slab only. The cap and nil_below are not shown to bidders, so the displayed winner fee % can differ from the amount actually charged.
RESEND API key is invalid in preview (401), so award-fee payer emails and admin/accounting notification emails are not delivered. Existing environment issue.

integration_issues.issue: Award-fee Stripe sessions show empty Buyer and Product / Fee columns (purpose 'award_fee' is not mapped to a label or buyer).

issues: Waive uses the browser's window.prompt for the reason. Use a shadcn Dialog with a textarea and validation (min 3 chars) instead.
Leaving the buyer email empty shows the generic toast 'Something went wrong · HTTP 422'. Validate on the client first and show an inline error on fee-plan-email.
The 422 error toast stays on screen next to the success toast after a successful Confirm fees.

action_items: Validate emd-masters bands against existing pricing_bands codes (422 for unknown codes)
Award fee: use the rule currency, or convert, when applying pct_max / nil_below to a bid priced in another currency
Replace window.prompt in AwardFeesPanel waive with a shadcn Dialog
Validate the buyer billing email on the client in FeePlanPanel; avoid the generic 'Something went wrong' toast
Label award_fee transactions in Billing > Payment transactions (Buyer / Product columns)
critical_code_review_comments: In bids.py the call to raise_award_fee is wrapped in try/except. If Stripe fails, _send_award_link raises HTTPException(502); the award still completes and link_error is stored. Good. It also means the award API gives no signal to the admin beyond the notification.
raise_award_fee returns None for notices published before this release (no fee_plan), so legacy awards never raise an award fee. Confirm this is intended.
waive_award_fee only allows status 'unpaid'. A 'nil' record cannot be waived, which is fine, but resend on 'nil' also returns 409 'Only unpaid' (verified).
seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST data only: TEST-FEE-{SUF}-n notices, TEST-BID-* bids, award_fees, TEST-VEN-* vendor, TEST_ emd rules, TEST-FEE-UI01 notice, TESTUIAF* award fee, testreg000000000000fee01 registration, and 2 award_fee payment_transactions created by Resend. All removed. The main agent's data (TEST-FEE-001, TEST_ Global award fee rule, TEST-BID-FEE award fee) is unchanged. REGIONAL band and tiers were restored to their original values. GLOBAL band was saved once from the UI with unchanged values (only updated_at changed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Admin UI login: POST /api/v1/admin/auth/login via fetch inside the page (the /admin/login page is a unified role picker with no admin-login testids), then go to /admin/e/{masters|notices|billing|registrations}. Run pytest with '-n 0' if needed. Stripe checkout creation works from the backend server (Resend link -> 200 'Payment link resent'); the Resend email API key is invalid. The award-fee tests call raise_award_fee in-process, where Stripe may fail with link_error; both outcomes are accepted.
